description: Redline streams live query metrics to any number of connected dashboards over WebSocket. The hub implements Go's fan-out pattern with an important detail: graceful backpressure handling that prevents one slow client from stalling the entire monitoring system.

text: In a monitoring tool, responsiveness is everything. If someone opens a dashboard on a slow connection or a tab goes to sleep, their WebSocket buffer fills up. Without backpressure handling, the broadcast loop blocks on that one client, and every other dashboard freezes. For a tool that is supposed to catch performance problems, becoming a performance problem itself is not an option.

codeSnippet.name: hub.go - Run()

text: The select with a default clause inside the broadcast loop is the critical piece. When sending to a client's buffered channel, if the channel is full (client is too slow), the default branch fires immediately - closing the client and removing it from the map. This is a non-blocking send. The hub never waits on any single client.

The RLock during broadcast allows multiple goroutines to read the client map concurrently while still protecting mutations through the full Lock on register/unregister. This means client connections and disconnections do not block active metric streaming.

list: Collector polls pg_stat_statements and pushes deltas into a channel
Hub receives from the broadcast channel and fans out to all connected clients
Each client has a buffered send channel (256 messages) - if it fills, the client is dropped
Clients register on WebSocket upgrade and unregister on disconnect
The entire pipeline is non-blocking - no goroutine ever waits on another
